data.name: Muridan
data.gender_notes: Muridan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'rada', meaning to return, reward, or provide. In Islamic context, Muridan is a name that conveys the idea of a benefactor, a provider, someone who returns favors and blessings. It is a reminder of Allah's mercy and blessings. The name Muridan carries the meaning “Benefactor, Provider” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muridan usually hope their child will grow to embody benefactor, provider and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes Allah's generosity and mercy.
data.etymology: Muridan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Benefactor, Provider.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muridan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference:
The Battle of Muridan took place in 632 AD during the Ridda Wars, a series of military campaigns led by Prophet Muhammad to suppress rebellions against Islamic rule in Arabia. The battle was fought against the Banu Muradah tribe who had renounced Islam and pledged allegiance to their tribal chieftain. The Prophet's forces, consisting mainly of the Muhajirun and Ansar, were led by Ali ibn Abi Talib. The battle resulted in a decisive victory for the Muslims, and the Banu Muradah tribe was forced to accept Islamic rule.
Context: Military campaign during the Ridda Wars.

Muradah ibn al-Mundhir was a prominent Quraysh tribesman and one of the early converts to Islam. He was a close companion of Prophet Muhammad and played a significant role in the early Islamic community. He was known for his generosity and piety, and his name is mentioned several times in Hadiths and Sira literature. Muradah was also an influential figure within the tribe of Quraysh, and used his position to promote Islam among his people.
Context: Early Islamic figure and companion of Prophet Muhammad.
